Scotts Bluff County sits in western Nebraska near the Wyoming border. Gering is the county seat, and Scottsbluff is the largest city. The county mixes farm land, river valleys, and the famous Scotts Bluff National Monument. This guide walks you through how the county tax sale works so you can plan safe tax lien investments.

What is / Brief Overview of County’s Tax Lien / Deed Investing

Scotts Bluff County uses a tax lien certificate system. It does not sell tax deeds at the auction stage. When owners miss real estate tax payments, the county sells tax lien certificates. You buy the lien and not the property. The owner can redeem by paying back taxes, fees, and interest. If they do not redeem in time, you may move toward foreclosure under Nebraska law.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • Scotts Bluff County uses a tax lien certificate system, selling liens rather than properties at auction.
  • The county’s annual tax sale occurs on the first Monday in March, requiring pre-registration before bidding.
  • Investors can earn high returns, around fourteen percent yearly, with a clear three-year redemption period.
  • Due diligence is crucial; buyers should research parcels to avoid pitfalls like vacant lots or unexpected liens.
  • Scotts Bluff County welcomes all investors, including out-of-state bidders, offering online tracking for certificates.

Fun Facts About the County

  • The county is named for a bluff that guided Oregon Trail travelers heading west.
  • Agriculture uses more than eighty percent of the land and includes both irrigated and pasture areas.
  • Sugar beets, dry beans, corn, and cattle play a major role in the local farm economy.
  • Scotts Bluff National Monument draws more than one hundred thousand visitors each year.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Attractions Scotts Bluff National Monument, Lake Minatare, Wildcat Hills, and North Platte National Wildlife Refuge.
  • Transportation Served by Highway 26, Highway 71, Highway 92, and the regional airport.
  • Economy Strong focus on crops, livestock, and food processing.
  • Community Outdoor recreation, small town living, and local colleges create steady demand for housing and services.

Why This County is Ideal for Tax Lien / Deed Investors

  • Nebraska tax lien certificates often pay high returns, around fourteen percent per year on redeemed liens.
  • The state sets clear rules, including a three-year redemption period.
  • The county offers many state tax lien opportunities across houses, rentals, and farm parcels.
  • Many investors see this as a low-risk investment compared to market swings.

Auction Process for Tax Lien / Deed Sales

Scotts Bluff County holds its tax lien sale on the first Monday in March at nine in the morning. It takes place at the County Administration Building on the top floor in Gering. Check-in begins at eight in the morning. The sale list appears for three weeks in February in the local newspaper and on Nebraska Taxes Online.

At the auction, you agree to buy the lien for the full delinquent amount plus fees. You also pay a certificate fee. Interest begins from the date of sale. The county does not bid down interest. Instead, it uses a Round Robin seat order.

How the Auction Works

Here is a simple step-by-step look at how the auction works on sale day.

  1. Complete Registration Before the Sale

    Turn in a registration form, W nine form, and the twenty five dollar fee by the Thursday before the sale.

  2. Receive Your Bidder Number

    The county assigns bidder numbers with a random generator.

  3. Follow the Parcel Order

    The Treasurer offers parcels starting from the highest dollar amount.

  4. Choose to Buy or Pass

    When your turn comes, you may buy or pass. If you pass, you wait for the next round.

  5. Pay Using an Approved Method

    Pay with cashier check, money order, or approved personal check with a bank letter.

  6. Watch for Remaining Parcels After the Sale

    After the public sale closes, remaining parcels move to private tax sale status for over the counter buying.

    Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Scotts Bluff County Tax Lien Certificates

    Nebraska law sets one interest rate for all counties. The simple interest rate is often around fourteen percent per year. Returns may change if the state updates the rate, so confirm each season. Your return depends on how long the owner takes to redeem. If they redeem fast, you earn interest on a short timeline. If they redeem near the end of three years, interest grows for a longer period.

    Many Nebraska tax lien certificates are redeemed. This means most investors expect interest income instead of property ownership. Clear rules and strong rates create steady expected returns.

    Open to All Investors and Foreign Investor Participation

    Any adult who meets registration rules may bid in Scotts Bluff County. You do not need to live in Nebraska. Out-of-state and international investors can join the sale. You must submit valid tax forms and payment in accepted formats.

    Investors from other states like Nebraska because they can track certificates online. Some foreign investors join through local agents or attorneys. Many like the fixed interest rate and clear redemption period.

    Importance of Due Diligence in Scotts Bluff County Tax Lien Investing

    Good research protects your money. Some parcels on the list may be vacant lots, flood areas, or older homes with repair needs. The county sells liens as is and does not promise clear title. Careful due diligence helps you avoid surprises after the sale.

    What Due Diligence Entails

    • Check the parcel on the county GIS map and confirm size and legal details.
    • Review aerial images and street views before bidding.
    • Look for other liens or mortgages in county records.
    • Check land use rules to be sure your plan fits the area.
    • Talk with a Nebraska attorney before foreclosure or quiet title actions.

    Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

    • You might buy a lien on land with no access or no use.
    • The property may have old utility bills or code cases.
    • Senior liens may survive and create extra costs.
    • Rehab or legal fees may exceed the final property value.

    Buying Over-the-Counter Liens in Scotts Bluff County

    After the public sale ends, unsold liens move into private tax sale status. This works like over-the-counter buying. You can request the list from the Treasurer’s office and pay the full amount due plus fees.

    How to Purchase OTC Liens or Deeds

    Ask the Treasurer for the current list. Confirm the parcel is still open. Pay the amount due and the certificate fee. The rules for redemption stay the same as those from the public sale. Always get written confirmation of total costs and terms.

    Benefits of OTC Purchases

    You avoid bidding in a room. You can move through the list at your own pace. Many large buyers skip small or remote parcels, which leaves more choices. The interest rate and redemption period match the public sale.

    Why Scotts Bluff County is a Top Choice for Tax Lien Investors

    Economic and Tax Advantages

    • A large share of agricultural land creates a steady tax lien inventory.
    • Irrigation history helps support land values.
    • Nebraska rules give a stable three-year redemption timeline.
    • Strong interest rates make these liens attractive compared with many other states.

    Real Estate Market Overview

    Property values in the county are modest. The area has a high owner occupancy rate. Farm land and small rentals provide a mix of parcel types. Lower price points allow investors to spread capital across many certificates.

    Conclusion

    Scotts Bluff County offers clear tax lien rules and strong interest rates. The annual sale happens in early March with a fair Round Robin process. The three year redemption period makes planning easier. Investors who take time to research parcels can earn steady interest and find long-term opportunities.

    Tax lien investing here works best when you study each parcel, understand county rules, and keep good records. With strong research and smart investing habits, these liens can support a steady real estate strategy.

    Pro Tips

    • Start with Nebraska Taxes Online and match parcels with county GIS maps.
    • Look for parcels where taxes are a small share of value.
    • Track each certificate in a simple spreadsheet.
    • Always check a property from the street or hire local help.
    • Keep a Nebraska attorney in your contacts for help with title or foreclosure steps.

    Scotts Bluff County Tax Sale FAQs

    Do I get the property right after the auction?

    No. You hold a lien. The owner keeps the property during redemption.

    Can I go inside the house before I buy a lien?

    No. You can only view from public areas or use online tools.

    What if the owner never redeems

    You can start foreclosure after the redemption period ends if you follow state rules.

    Can I use financing to buy liens?

    Most investors use cash or bank funds because the county needs a certified payment.

    Can I sell my certificate later?

    Yes. Nebraska allows the assignment of certificates for a small fee.
